subject: Elysium dedicated capacity — preliminary slab sizing & traffic shaping
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@elysium.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: lena@elysium.ai
Date: Mon, Apr 05, 2027 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Elysium prod needs

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team is getting pushed to put an SLA around the new assistant and we need a concrete starting point for a Dedicated (reserved) capacity discussion. High level details: 
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~120 reqs/min, typical request = prompt 120 tokens + generation 220 tokens (avg).
- Peak profile: brief bursts up to ~1,200 reqs/min for marketing campaigns (10x baseline) lasting ~10–20 minutes.
- Latency SLO: P95 generation end-to-end <= 400ms for the majority of flows; some lower-priority flows can be best-effort.
- Model preference: Llama2-chat-like family (we're evaluating 13B and 33B variants).
- Cache: we will have a warm KV cache for conversational sessions but new chat storms will produce cold starts.

Can you provide: a rough tokens/sec estimate per GPU for our model flavors (FP16 and 4-bit), recommended slab sizing for a starting reserved commit (including headroom for peaks), and any operational controls we should plan for (traffic shaping, burst policies, fallbacks)?

Appreciate anything you can share quickly — procurement is already asking for a timeline for a formal proposal.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Platform
Elysium AI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@elysium.ai>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, Apr 05, 2027 at 11:05 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Elysium prod needs

Samir —

Thanks for the detail — this is exactly what we need to start. High-level answers up front, then a few clarifying Qs so the slab numbers line up with what you actually ship: 

Quick top-line (very rough): 
- Llama2-13B-like
  - FP16: ~60–80 tokens/sec per high-end A100-like GPU under our optimized runtime for single-request low-batch latency paths.
  - 4-bit quantized: ~110–160 tokens/sec per GPU (depends on kernel set / model ops).
- Llama2-33B-like
  - FP16: ~25–40 tokens/sec per GPU.
  - 4-bit: ~50–85 tokens/sec per GPU.

From that, and using your nominal request size (~340 tokens total), we estimate sustained single-GPU throughput (requests/sec) of roughly: 13B-FP16 ~0.18–0.23 r/s, 13B-4bit ~0.32–0.47 r/s. Peak bursts will require horizontal headroom rather than pushing single-GPU latency.

Recommended starting slab (very conservative, with ~40% burst headroom): 
- 13B on 4-bit quant: 8 GPUs reserved — supports ~2.6–3.8 r/s aggregate steady, with burst absorb to ~5–6 r/s for short windows (maps to ~300–360 reqs/min). To hit 1,200 reqs/min bursts, you'd need additional ephemeral burst capacity or a larger commit (we can model a burst-only pool).
- 33B on 4-bit quant: 12 GPUs reserved — supports ~1.0–1.5 r/s steady, with similar burst multipliers.

Operational controls we recommend: 
1) Priority routing: pin high-SLA flows to a reserved subset and leave best-effort to shared hosted capacity.
2) Burst pool + graceful degradation: keep a small reserved slab + autoscale to a burst pool (or prebook extra slabs for marketing windows).
3) Request shaping: enforce generation token caps per request during bursts, and queue small lower-priority requests for cold-cache warmups.

Couple clarifying Qs so Olga and I can produce a fleshed-out XLS with scenarios (we'll attach it):
- Do the 1,200 reqs/min bursts represent mostly short single-token follow-ups, or full-length generations?
- What is your acceptable max p95 under peak (if 400ms can't hold, are you okay with 800–1,000ms briefly)?
- Any hard constraints on quantization/accuracy tradeoffs?

I've attached a brief assumptions PDF and an initial slab scenario workbook — Olga will follow up with per-GPU latency math and a recommended traffic shaping plan. If procurement needs pricing placeholders to sketch a PO, we can include that in the formal proposal.

Ben
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: elysium_sizing_assumptions.pdf (PDF, 42 KB), initial-slab-scenario.xlsx (XLSX, 85 KB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@elysium.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, Apr 06, 2027 at 10:18 AM -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Elysium prod needs

Samir / team —

Following Ben's top-line, here are more concrete per-GPU modeling assumptions and a recommended slab & traffic-shaping playbook. I've included the math inline so you can sanity-check quickly.

Assumptions (runtime tuned):
- Model: we benchmarked a 13B-chat variant and scaled numbers for 33B using measured layer counts.
- Typical request: 120 prompt + 220 gen = 340 tokens.
- Kernel latency measured is per-token after warmup; prefix processing adds a fixed ~25–40ms depending on sequence length.
- Target p95 budget: 400ms for generation portion; end-to-end includes other infra (network, app) so leaves ~350–380ms for runtime on a warm request.

Measured numbers (representative):
- 13B-FP16: 70 tokens/sec median; p95 single-request path ~90–95ms per 100 tokens (so 340 tokens ~310–325ms).
- 13B-4bit: 130 tokens/sec median; p95 ~60–70ms per 100 tokens (340 tokens ~205–240ms).
- 33B-FP16: 32 tokens/sec median; p95 ~150–180ms per 100 tokens (340 tokens ~510–610ms — misses SLO for p95).
- 33B-4bit: 68 tokens/sec median; p95 ~85–100ms per 100 tokens (340 tokens ~290–340ms — close to SLO).

Tokens/sec -> requests/sec conversion example (13B-4bit): 130 tokens/sec GPU -> 130 / 340 = 0.382 r/s per GPU -> ~22.9 r/min per GPU.

Slab sizing scenarios (goal: maintain P95 <= 400ms during baseline and give 3x short burst headroom, plus operational margin):
- Baseline traffic (~120 req/min = 2 r/s): For 13B-4bit, baseline needs ~0.17 GPUs (2 r/s / 0.382 r/s per GPU) => practically 1 GPU for baseline.
- Practical reserved commit recommendation: start with 6 GPUs (13B-4bit). Rationale: 6 GPUs provide ~2.3 r/s steady aggregate (137 r/min) and allow short-burst absorption to ~6–7 r/s with internal queueing and shaping (maps to ~360–420 reqs/min). Add ephemeral burst capacity to handle the 1,200 req/min marketing peak and cap generation tokens during those bursts to preserve p95 for priority flows.

- If you choose 33B-4bit, start with 10 GPUs. 10 GPUs -> ~3.8 r/s steady (~230 r/min), burst to ~11–12 r/s with shaping (~660–720 r/min).

Operational controls we recommend implementing immediately:
1) Priority lanes: tag requests by SLA and route high-priority to the reserved slab. Low-priority traffic can be routed to shared-hosted or delayed.
2) Pre-warm strategy: do a rolling cache-warm cycle for active sessions during expected campaign windows (preemptively warm top ~5k hot prompts).
3) Burst-steering + token caps: implement an automated token cap policy when 90% of slab utilization is reached — reduce max generation tokens to 120 for non-critical requests.
4) Canary + can-shed: deploy a canary fleet (2 GPUs) that receives 5% of production traffic to validate quantization impact in prod prior to full cutover.

Headroom math summary (13B-4bit, 6 GPUs):
- Median tokens/sec per GPU: 130 -> aggregate median 780 t/s -> aggregate r/s = 780 / 340 = 2.29 r/s -> ~137 r/min steady.
- Safe burst absorb (with shaping + queueing): ~3x steady -> ~411 r/min (short windows).

Notes on accuracy vs quantization: 4-bit gives ~1.8-2x throughput improvement over FP16 in our stacks but increases variance slightly on p95. We can run an eval set you provide to quantify any class-level regressions and include fallback to FP16 for flows that must not degrade.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben/Marissa: I'll take the attached XLS and produce two concrete commit options (A: 6-gpu 13B-4bit + burst pool; B: 10-gpu 33B-4bit) with estimated monthly cost, expected p95 performance, and a canary rollout plan.
- Samir: if you can confirm burst composition (full gens vs short follow-ups) and any accuracy constraints, I'll tighten the numbers.

Drive folder with full simulation results: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBz-Elysium-simulations

Olga Petrov
Staff SE, Inference Performance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Elysium prod needs

Thanks — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. We're comfortable starting with the 13B-4bit path for initial launch and running an eval on accuracy against our prompt set. Procurement is copied to start the commercial discussion — they'd like preliminary pricing and a mutual action plan (timeline, milestones, canary dates).

Action items from Elysium side:
- Lena will send a 2k-sample eval prompt set by EOD Thu.
- Procurement will send a short procurement checklist and PO timeline in the next 48 hours.

Ben / Olga — please send the two formal options and a suggested MA P (mutual action plan) by Friday so we can lock dates.

Best,
Samir
